product.reading: Reading what Falco saw on your hosts.

detectionsPage.title: Detections
detectionsPage.description: Falco's rules matching on {{hosts}} hosts · {{policies}} policies
detectionsPage.noHostsDetail: Make an enrolment token under Hosts, then start runtime-agent next to Falco on each host. Setup has the configuration.
detectionsPage.perHourDetail: Falco's alerts by severity, last 24 hours
detectionsPage.search: Search rules, hosts, containers or processes
detectionsPage.selectRow: Select a row to see its process tree
detectionsPage.noneDetail: Nothing matched a Falco rule in alert mode here.
detectionsPage.falsePositiveDetail: Say why, so the next person knows. The detection stops collecting; the next match opens a new one. To stop a rule from raising detections, turn its policy off.

eventsPage.title: Events
eventsPage.description: Every alert Falco sent from your hosts, kept for the retention period, whether it raised a detection or not.
eventsPage.ofDetection: Showing the events of one detection
eventsPage.search: Text in the output, rule, host or container
eventsPage.resultHelp: Alerted events raised or joined a detection; kept ones matched a rule whose policy is off.
eventsPage.kept: Kept without a detection: this rule's policy is off.

processesPage.title: Processes
processesPage.description: What ran where and what started it, counted from Falco's program starts and compared with what each host or image ran before.
processesPage.learningDetail: Everything this host runs until then is taken as normal. Afterwards a program it never ran is new, and a known program with a new parent or user is drift.
processesPage.baselineHelp: Known: learned or accepted. New: a program this host or image never ran. Drift: a known program with a parent or user never seen with it.
processesPage.noneDetail: Load runtime-agent's Falco rule OpenAsy process started to count program starts. See Setup.

filesPage.title: File integrity
filesPage.description: Changes to the files that should never change: accounts, sudo, SSH, cron, the loader and system binaries, read by the agent on each host and compared with the read before.
filesPage.noneDetail: The watched files are as the agents first read them.
filesPage.unknownProcess: Falco saw no process write it

done.approved: Approved; the new state is the baseline

policiesPage.title: Policies
policiesPage.description_one: {{count}} rule seen: what each does when it matches
policiesPage.description_other: {{count}} rules seen: what each does when it matches
policiesPage.falcoRulesDetail: Falco matches its rules on each host; Runtime decides what a match does. Alert opens a detection; off keeps the event and raises nothing. A rule appears here when it first matches.
policiesPage.modeHelp: Alert opens a detection. Off keeps the event only.
policiesPage.noneDetail: A rule is listed when Falco first sends a match for it.

hostsPage.title: Hosts
hostsPage.description: Every host with Falco and runtime-agent. The agent sends what Falco sees and reads the watched files; it never runs anything Runtime sends.
hostsPage.silentDetail: The agent has not called Runtime for two minutes. The host may be down, cut off, or the agent stopped.
hostsPage.sensorDownDetail: The agent cannot reach Falco's web server; no events come from this host.
hostsPage.removeDetail: Its agent's secret ends at once and the name is free to enrol again. Its detections and events stay; its program inventory and watched files go.
hostsPage.noneDetail: Make an enrolment token below and start the agent with it.
hostsPage.tokensDetail: An agent trades a token once for a secret of its own. Use one per host, or one with more uses for a fleet such as a DaemonSet. Tokens last 7 days.
hostsPage.maxUsesHint: How many hosts may enrol with it
hostsPage.tokenOnce: Copy the token now: it is not shown again

setupPage.title: Setup
setupPage.description: Falco watches each host with eBPF; runtime-agent next to it sends what Falco sees to Runtime.
setupPage.falcoDetail: Falco 0.39 or newer, with its modern eBPF probe, on Linux 5.8 or newer. Send its alerts as JSON to the agent, turn on its web server for health, and ask for the fields that make a process tree. Load runtime-agent's rules file too, for the process inventory.
setupPage.agentDetail: One per host, or a DaemonSet in Kubernetes. Make an enrolment token under Hosts and start the agent with it once; afterwards it uses its own secret.
setupPage.siemDetail: Set these on Runtime to send each new detection and file change to OpenAsy SIEM as an event.
setupPage.siemOn: Sending new detections and file changes to SIEM at {{url}}.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Runtime.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Runtime, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also work detections, review file changes and accept programs; admins also change policies, enrol and remove hosts, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
